boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Dallas record (May 26-June 1, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The main action is Bate's attack on the Fifteenth Corps on May 28; New Hope Church (GA010) and Pickett's Mill (GA012) are separate records on the same lines, and the withdrawal from Dallas after June 1 is context. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the Military Division of Mississippi and the Army of Tennessee without counts; the live field reads zero. Logan says the attack of the 28th was made by Hardee's entire command, which prisoners estimated at 25,000. Cox says Hardee sent Bate's division out on a forced reconnaissance, its three brigades in separate columns, and that Union superiority in numbers let the entrenchments be held with part of the force. NPS says Hardee's corps probed the line.
claims.rationale: Prisoners' estimate against a history naming one division; no count of troops engaged is inspected and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Cox says the attack was repulsed after half an hour with terrible loss, and Logan that line after line was sent back broken. Logan says the enemy had evacuated his works by daylight on June 5, after the frozen interval.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The June 5 evacuation is later context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 5,400 (US 2,400; CS 3,000); the live field reads 1880 (US 380; CS 1500). Logan reports his corps' loss as 30 killed, 295 wounded and 54 missing, aggregate 379; says he took 97 prisoners and buried over 300 Confederate dead; and estimates the enemy loss at 2,000. Cox repeats Logan's figures, says the Sixteenth Corps losses were not separately enumerated, and notes Johnston's statement of Bate's loss as some three hundred killed and wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Logan's 379 covers the Fifteenth Corps only; the live US 380 is close to it, but the frozen US 2,400 has no inspected basis.

open_questions: McPherson's May 28 dispatches, Dodge's and Harrow's reports, Bate's and Hardee's accounts, Johnston's report (not a family here) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Logan's Fifteenth Corps reports, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, are a third family (interested Union accounts). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
